findings.title: Task 8's consumer check has a positive answer that no task acts on
findings.description: Task 8 tells the implementer to extend `sdk_session.dispatch`'s `sdk_type` exclusion tuple and then to "verify no other `sdk_type` exclusion list exists elsewhere in the codebase … (grep for `SDK_RESULT_TYPE` across `src/`)". That grep does return others: `src/squadron/review/review_client.py:263` (`if sdk_type in (SDK_RESULT_TYPE, "tool_use", "tool_result"): continue`), `src/squadron/pipeline/summary_oneshot.py:139`, and `src/squadron/metrology/audit.py:542-557`. All of these consume translated messages from the **agent** paths (`_handle_query_mode` / `_handle_client_mode`), which Task 4 makes newly observable — before the slice, translation returned `[]` for `RateLimitEvent`; after it, an informational event becomes one `MessageType.system` message that these filters do not exclude and will therefore append into review prose. The gap this leaves unmet is the slice's own issue-#23 defect class on the review/summary/one-shot paths, and it is the exact thing Task 14 claims to check ("no `rate_limit_event` text appears in the artifact's prose") with nothing in the plan guaranteeing it. Additionally, Task 4 never specifies the new `Message.content`, so the implementer has no basis for deciding whether this message is prose-carrying. Fix: give Task 8 an outcome for a positive grep hit (extend those tuples, or state that the translated rate-limit message is metadata-only/empty-content and therefore inert), or add a small task naming the four consumer sites.

findings.title: Test rewrites trail their implementation by two tasks; two commits land with a red suite
findings.description: Task 6 commits after removing the `is_rate_limit_event(exc.data)` special case, but `test_a_rejected_rate_limit_event_reaches_the_backoff` (tests/providers/sdk/test_agent.py:648) still fabricates a `MessageParseError` carrying a `rate_limit_event` payload and asserts backoff — from Task 6's commit onward that event is skipped, so the test fails. Task 9 then commits after deleting `install_rate_limit_parser_shim`, while the four `test_the_shim_*` tests (tests/providers/sdk/test_agent.py:684-763) still import it — those become collection errors. Both are repaired only in Task 10. So two of the thirteen commit points are not at working, tested points, and the test-with pattern is broken for Tasks 6/7/8 (their tests are Tasks 10/11, with intervening commits between). Fix: fold the four shim-test deletions into Task 9, and either move the `test_agent.py` rewrite to immediately after Task 6 or merge Task 6+7+8+9's rewrite into a single commit-bearing unit that lands green. (The pattern is otherwise correct: Task 3 follows Task 2, Task 5 follows Task 4.)

findings.title: Task 6 says "replace both gates" where `agent.py` has three `RATE_LIMIT_MARKER` sites
findings.description: Task 6 reads: "replace both `RATE_LIMIT_MARKER in str(exc)` gates (in `_handle_query_mode` and `_handle_client_mode`) with `_is_throttle(exc)`." In the file there are two gates inside `_handle_query_mode` — the retry gate at line 167 and the **error-type selection** gate at line 180 (`if RATE_LIMIT_MARKER in str(exc): raise ProviderRateLimitError ... else raise ProviderError`) — plus one in `_handle_client_mode` at line 216, and one in `sdk_session.dispatch` at line 192 (Task 7). "Both" invites a junior implementer to change only the retry gates and leave line 180 keyed on the substring. The requirement that leaves unmet is Success Criterion 6: post-slice, whether a budget-exhausted `RateLimitRejected` becomes `ProviderRateLimitError` depends on the message text chosen at the new raise site (the existing raise inherits `MessageParseError`'s "Unknown message type: rate_limit_event" text, which contained the marker; a hand-written raise message may not). Partial backstop: Task 10's rewrite of `test_exhausted_rate_limit_raises_a_distinct_error` asserts `ProviderRateLimitError` on the query-mode path, so it would catch the omission — but only if that test is pointed at query mode as it is today. Recommend Task 6 name the three agent.py lines (or say "every `RATE_LIMIT_MARKER in str(exc)` occurrence in the file, including the error-type selection at the tail of `_handle_query_mode`"). Note also, for accuracy rather than as a gap: client mode's exhausted-budget path raises through the outer handler and becomes `ProviderError`, not `ProviderRateLimitError`, both before and after the slice; that is unchanged behavior and consistent with criterion 6's "still", but it means criterion 6's audit clause is not exercised end-to-end by any task (T12 only confirms two CLI-plumbing tests that construct `AuditRunResult` directly).

findings.title: Criterion 3's `RateLimitStats.throttles` increment has no task on the pipeline path
findings.description: Criterion 3 states that a `rejected` event reaching *any* of the three dispatch paths triggers backoff, "`RateLimitStats.throttles` increments and a WARNING is logged naming the attempt number." `SDKExecutionSession.dispatch` has no `RateLimitStats` at all — it imports only `MAX_RATE_LIMIT_RETRIES`, `RATE_LIMIT_MARKER`, `install_rate_limit_parser_shim`, `rate_limit_backoff_s` (src/squadron/pipeline/sdk_session.py:33-38) and logs the WARNING without recording stats; the LLD meanwhile lists "`RateLimitStats` accumulation" under **Unchanged**. Tasks 7 and 11 follow the LLD, not criterion 3, so the third path satisfies the WARNING and the retry but never the stats clause. The unmet requirement is criterion 3 as literally written. Fix is a one-line reconciliation: either narrow criterion 3 (or the task's success line) to "agent paths record stats; the pipeline path logs and retries as today", or add a step to Task 7/11 that asserts what the pipeline path actually reports.

findings.title: Tasks trace cleanly to the design's decisions and probe findings
findings.description: D1→T9, D2→T1 (floor only, no ceiling, with the rationale cited rather than restated), D3→T2 (single `_STATUS_REJECTED` definition, typed field read rather than `.raw`), D4→T2/T6/T7, D5→T6/T7 docstring rewrites with the `MessageParseError` branch explicitly retained, D6→T4/T8. The asymmetric pipeline path the design calls "the most likely place for the slice to half-land" gets its own task (T7) with the reason it cannot be shared with T6 stated. Criterion 9 is enforced structurally: T10 and T11 carry grep-based completion checks for the fabricated-exception patterns, and the Notes section forbids `MagicMock(spec=RateLimitEvent)` stand-ins. T12's out-of-scope guard on `tests/providers/openai/test_agent.py` correctly implements the accepted F007 correction.

findings.title: Minor verifiability and granularity points
findings.description:
- T3's `pytest -k "classif or throttle or RateLimitRejected"` selects on test names not yet fixed; a zero-match run collects nothing. Citing the new test node ids (or just running the file) makes the gate concrete.
- T5 says create `tests/providers/sdk/test_translation.py` "if it does not exist" — it already exists (tests/providers/sdk/test_translation.py), so the conditional is dead but harmless.
- T9's success grep is `src` only, while criterion 2 and the LLD walkthrough step 1 grep `src tests`; the `tests/` half is satisfied by T10's deletions, so widening T9's grep to `src tests` would just be clearer about who proves what.
- T12 modifies no source and its `pytest tests/providers/sdk/test_provider.py tests/metrology/test_audit_cli.py` run is subsumed by T13's `pytest tests/providers tests/metrology`; it could be merged into T13, with its "don't touch the OpenAI file" guard and DEVLOG note moving with it. This is the only granularity trim I'd suggest — 16 tasks for this slice is proportionate, since the design states the cost is in test rewriting and live verification, and T14/T15 are mandated by the walkthrough.
- No load test is required or implied: this slice restates no NFR, and the "throughput collapse under load" risk is covered by the live audit (T15) plus the forced-throttle observation, which is the appropriate proxy. Consequently no CI-gating task is owed.
- Commit markers (13 of 16 tasks) sit at task boundaries per CLAUDE.md's once-per-task rule; their absence at T12/T14/T15 is correct, since those tasks change nothing to commit and T15 explicitly must revert its injection.
